name: Mikhail Bakunin
role: Russian revolutionary and collectivist anarchist theorist (1814–1876)
summary: Bakunin’s mature politics sought to abolish the state and capitalist ownership in favor of freely federated communes and workers’ associations. He defended material equality, women’s emancipation and secular education while advocating mass revolution and clandestine organization. His polemics also made antisemitic conspiracy allegations.

notes: No inferred answers. Downloaded full program, book chapters, educational essays, economic fragment and organizational letters; searched across statement themes. Mature anarchism takes precedence over early pan-Slav nationalism. Public ownership means social ownership by producers, not nationalization. Equality does not imply identical outcomes; collectivism does not establish abolition of money or distribution exclusively by need. The 1866 text retains transitional parliamentary and judicial provisions, so it does not establish every later anarchist institutional demand. The archive incorrectly labels its 1866 Catechism header as an 1851 prison text; its content and editorial introduction identify the actual work. It is distinct from Nechayev’s 1869 Catechism of a Revolutionary. The 1870 letter rejects coercing comrades while permitting manipulation of enemies: methods/ends is therefore qualified, and covert organization is not treated as support for a ruling state party. Antisemitic allegations are recorded alongside egalitarian principles without inventing a policy of legal racial segregation. Ecology, modern technology and modern identity-policy specifics are left null. Abolishing state police and criminal codes is not expanded into a claim about abolishing every prison; common landownership is not equated with requiring collective farming.
